parts.context: Sarah, an office manager, talks to Hassan, a network engineer, about the network for a new office.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Hassan, thanks for coming. As you know, we're opening a small office in Hai Phong next month. What kind of network do we need there?

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: It's a small office with eight people, so a simple LAN is fine. I'd suggest wired connections for the desks, because they're faster and more reliable, and wi-fi for the meeting room.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Do they need their own server?

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: No. A server is expensive to look after. They can use the server which we have here in Hanoi. They'll connect to it through a VPN.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: Yes. A VPN encrypts all the data that goes between the two offices. If someone steals the data, they won't be able to read it.

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: One network printer is enough. If everyone connects to it, we won't need a separate printer on each desk.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: How long will the installation take?

script.speaker: Hassan
script.text: About three days. I'm finishing a job in Vinh this week, so I can start on the fifteenth.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Great. Can you send me a price by Friday?

The old network in Hanoi is too slow.
Eight new people are joining the Hanoi office.

options.text: It only works in the meeting room.

It encrypts the data between the two offices.

parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and answer the questions. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer (Questions L6–L10).
parts.context: Owen from IT Services explains the student portal to new university students.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: Good afternoon. I'm Owen from IT Services, and I'm going to tell you how to use the student portal, which is the website where you'll find your timetable, your grades and your course materials. You'll use it every day, so save the address in your browser.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: To log in, use your student number, which is on your student card, and the password that we sent you by text message. The first time you log in, the portal asks you to choose a new password. It must have at least ten characters.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: The portal works best in Chrome or Firefox. If a page looks strange or doesn't load, clear your browser history and try again. If that doesn't help, contact us through the help page.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: One more thing: please always log out when you use a computer in the library, so that nobody else can see your grades.

questions.stem: Where can students find their student number?
questions.explanation: "use your student number, which is on your student card".

questions.stem: How did the university send students their first password?
questions.explanation: "the password that we sent you by text message".

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of characters for the new password?
questions.explanation: "It must have at least ten characters."

questions.stem: What should students clear if a page does not load?
questions.explanation: "If a page looks strange or doesn't load, clear your browser history and try again."

questions.stem: Where must students always log out of the portal?
questions.explanation: "please always log out when you use a computer in the library, so that nobody else can see your grades".

matching.instructions: Match the terms (1–5) with the correct definitions (A–F). There is one extra definition that you do not need (Questions 1–5).

definitions.text: A copy of something presented in a form that can be read on a computer.
A rule or instruction about the best way to do something.
Connected together using pieces of thin metal in the form of threads.
To attach a computer code to a word, phrase, image, etc. in order to arrange the data in a particular way.
A circuit that connects the main parts of a computer so that signals can be sent from one part to another.

items.explanation: Guideline (hướng dẫn, nguyên tắc chỉ dẫn) là quy tắc hay chỉ dẫn về cách tốt nhất để làm việc gì.
Tag (gắn thẻ) là gắn một mã máy tính vào từ, cụm từ, hình ảnh… để sắp xếp dữ liệu theo một cách nhất định.
Bus (bus, đường truyền) là mạch nối các bộ phận chính của máy tính để tín hiệu đi từ bộ phận này sang bộ phận khác.
Back button (nút quay lại) là nút trên trình duyệt để trở về trang trước.
Electronic version (bản điện tử) là bản sao ở dạng đọc được trên máy tính. Định nghĩa C là của wired (có dây), không có trong danh sách thuật ngữ.

grammar.stem: Look! The printer ______ the same page again and again.
grammar.explanation: "Look!" cho thấy việc đang xảy ra ngay lúc nói: hiện tại tiếp diễn. Chủ ngữ số ít (The printer) nên "is printing".

grammar.stem: This laptop ______ to the sales department, not to us.
grammar.explanation: "belong" là động từ trạng thái, không dùng ở thì tiếp diễn. Chủ ngữ số ít nên "belongs".

grammar.stem: The laptop ______ I bought last month is already too slow.
grammar.explanation: Mệnh đề quan hệ bổ nghĩa cho vật (The laptop): dùng "which" (hoặc that). "who" chỉ dùng cho người.

grammar.stem: Staff ______ work from home need to use the VPN.
grammar.explanation: Mệnh đề quan hệ bổ nghĩa cho người (Staff) làm chủ ngữ của "work": dùng "who".

grammar.stem: If you press Ctrl and Z, the computer ______ your last action.
grammar.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 0 cho điều luôn đúng: If + hiện tại đơn, hiện tại đơn (undoes).

grammar.stem: If the new laptops ______ on Friday, we will set them up next week.
grammar.explanation: Câu điều kiện loại 1: mệnh đề If dùng hiện tại đơn; chủ ngữ số nhiều (the new laptops) nên "arrive", không dùng "will".

grammar.stem: There is ______ USB port on the left side of the laptop.
grammar.explanation: USB đọc bắt đầu bằng âm /juː/ (phụ âm) nên dùng "a", không dùng "an". any / much không đi với danh từ đếm được số ít trong câu khẳng định này.

vocabulary.stem: ______ the link at the bottom of the email to read the full article on our website.
vocabulary.explanation: Follow a link (nhấp vào đường liên kết để đi tới trang mà nó dẫn đến).

vocabulary.stem: Please ______ the delivery form to show that you have received the parcel.
vocabulary.explanation: Sign (ký) là viết chữ ký lên giấy tờ để xác nhận.

vocabulary.stem: I left my ______ at home, so I can't charge my phone today.
vocabulary.explanation: Recharger (bộ sạc) là thiết bị nạp điện lại cho pin.

vocabulary.stem: We scanned the old paper documents and used ______ software to change them into text that we can edit.
vocabulary.explanation: OCR (nhận dạng ký tự quang học) là phần mềm nhận ra chữ và số trên giấy để đưa tài liệu giấy vào máy tính.

vocabulary.stem: The calculator app has all the basic ______, such as adding, subtracting and multiplying.
vocabulary.explanation: Function (chức năng) là một thao tác cơ bản máy tính thực hiện, ví dụ cộng, trừ, nhân.

vocabulary.stem: Our technicians can fix most software problems ______, so they don't need to visit your office.
vocabulary.explanation: Remotely (từ xa): kỹ thuật viên sửa lỗi từ xa nên không cần đến văn phòng.

vocabulary.stem: All the team leaders will ______ in a discussion about the new network next Monday.
vocabulary.explanation: Take part in (tham gia) một hoạt động cùng người khác.

vocabulary.stem: The clinic keeps a ______ of every patient visit on the computer.
vocabulary.explanation: Record (hồ sơ, bản ghi) là thông tin được ghi lại hoặc lưu trên máy tính để xem sau này.

passage.title: Smartphones on the Farm
paragraphs: Gareth Jones has a dairy farm with 150 cows in north Wales. Five years ago, he did all his paperwork at the kitchen table in the evening. Today, he does most of it on his smartphone while he is working in the fields.

Each cow wears a small sensor on its collar. The sensor measures how much the cow moves and sends the information to an app on Gareth's phone. If a cow moves much less than usual, it is often ill, so the app warns him immediately. 'I'm finding problems two or three days earlier than before,' Gareth says. 'If I find a problem early, the vet's bill is much smaller.'

The farm also has sensors in the fields which measure how wet the soil is. Every morning, Gareth checks these readings before he decides where the cows will go that day. When he needs animal food, he orders it with another app, which shows him the prices of three different companies.

There are still some problems. The mobile signal on parts of the farm is weak, so the sensors cannot always send their data. Gareth is solving this by putting a small wi-fi mast on the roof of his barn. 'Farming is still hard work,' he says, 'but my phone saves me about ten hours a week. If I'm not doing paperwork in the evening, I can spend more time with my family.'

questions.stem: How is Gareth solving the problem with the weak mobile signal?

options.text: He is buying a new phone.
He is putting a wi-fi mast on the roof of his barn.
He is moving the sensors closer to the house.
He is doing the paperwork in the evening again.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: "Gareth is solving this by putting a small wi-fi mast on the roof of his barn."

passage.title: Network maintenance this Saturday
paragraphs: Our network provider is upgrading the equipment in the server room this Saturday, 14th June, from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. During this time, the internet, email and the shared drives will not be available. We chose Saturday because very few people work at the weekend.
If you need to work at the weekend, please download the files that you need before you leave on Friday. The VPN will also be offline, so you won't be able to connect from home.

The phone system uses a separate line, so it will work as normal. Customers can still call the helpdesk, but technicians won't be able to open customer accounts until the work is finished. If there is an urgent problem on Saturday, please call my mobile.
Please switch off your computer before you leave on Friday, but don't unplug it. If a computer is still on, the update restarts it automatically, and you may lose any work that you haven't saved.

bullets: this month: lots of staff / take their summer holidays
open your email program / click 'File', then 'Automatic Replies'
type a short message (give the date when you'll be back)
add the name of a colleague (this person can help while you're away)

targetGrammar: Present continuous for something happening now or around now: Lots of staff are taking their holidays this month
Relative clauses with which, that or who: a message which gives…, a colleague who can help…
Zero or first conditional: If you only want to reply to…, tick… / If someone writes to you, they will…
Imperatives with sequence words for the steps
email.modelAnswer:
From: Hoang Minh Chau
To: Olivia
Date: 2nd July
Subject: Automatic replies

Hi Olivia,

Many staff are taking holidays this month.
It should be quite easy to set up an automatic reply.
First, open your email program and click 'File', then 'Automatic Replies'.
Then, select 'Send automatic replies'.
Next, type a short message which gives the date when you'll be back.
After that, add the name of a colleague who can help while you're away.
Finally, just tick 'Inside my organisation only'. If you do, only colleagues will get the reply.
Don't forget to click 'OK' when you've finished.

Best wishes,
Hoang Minh Chau
IT Officer
IT Department

parts.instructions: Answer the three questions. Speak for 30–45 seconds for each question.
questions: What device do you use most, and what are you using it for most this week? Use the present simple for things you usually do and the present continuous for things you are doing now or this week.
What happens if you leave a phone in the hot sun or drop it in water? Use zero conditional sentences (If you…, the phone…).
What kinds of messages and files do you usually send to your teachers or friends? Use relative clauses with which, that or who (I send photos which…, I write to friends who…).

parts.instructions: Explain the parts of a web browser. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Your uncle has just started using the internet. Explain what each part of a web browser in the cues is and what it does. Use relative clauses with which, that or who (The address bar is the box which…, A tab is something that…).
requiredGrammar: Relative clauses with which, that or who: The address bar is the box which…, A tab is something that…
parts.sampleAnswer: Let me show you the main parts of the browser. At the top, there's the address bar, which is the long box where you type the address of a website. Next to it, there's the back button. It's the arrow that takes you to the page which you were looking at before. The refresh button is the one which loads the page again when it isn't working properly. A bookmark is a way of saving a website that you visit often, so you don't have to type the address every time. Finally, tabs are the small boxes at the top which let you open several websites in the same window. For example, you can read the news in one tab and check the weather in another.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: A friend owns a small café and is not sure whether to offer free wi-fi to customers. Explain the benefits and the risks, and give your advice. Use first conditional sentences (If you offer…, customers will…) and at least one zero conditional sentence (If many people stream videos, the network…).
cues: customers stay longer / buy more drinks and food
students and people who work online choose your café
risk: if many people stream videos, the connection gets slow
advice: a separate guest network keeps the café's computer safe / change the password every week
requiredGrammar: First conditional: If you offer free wi-fi, customers will…
Zero conditional: If many people stream videos, the connection gets slow
parts.sampleAnswer: I think free wi-fi is a good idea for your café. If you offer free wi-fi, customers will stay longer, and if they stay longer, they'll probably buy more drinks and food. Also, if students and people who work online know about it, they'll choose your café instead of the one across the road. But there are some risks. If a lot of people stream videos at the same time, the connection gets very slow, and then customers complain. So my advice is to set up a separate guest network. If customers use the guest network, they can't see your till or your office computer, so your data stays safe. And please change the password every week. If you do that, people outside the café won't use your connection all day.
